title: Receive a signal
subtitle: NULL dereference → page fault → SIGSEGV → shell message
why_it_matters: Signals are how the kernel reports asynchronous events to userspace. A bad memory access must not hang the machine — it must classify the fault, deliver SIGSEGV, reap the child, and return control to the shell.

dual_view.kernel:
#PF (not present, user)
  ↓ pf_user_segv
  ↓ SIGSEGV default kill
  ↓ process_exit → zombie
  ↓ wait4 → WIFSIGNALED

steps.label: Bad access
steps.what_ir0_does: User code touches unmapped or forbidden virtual address. CPU raises #PF.
steps.why_it_matters: Every segfault story starts in ring 3.

steps.label: CPU #PF
steps.what_ir0_does: x86-64 saves error code and faulting address (CR2). Vector dispatches to mm_page_fault_handle.
steps.why_it_matters: Architecture frame is evidence — not optional logging.

steps.label: Classify fault
steps.what_ir0_does: Demand paging, COW, or pf_user_segv when access is invalid. Smoke uses 0xDEADBEEF deliberately.
steps.why_it_matters: Same handler serves growth and crashes — classification must be exact.

steps.label: SIGSEGV
steps.what_ir0_does: Default action kills the process when no handler is installed. Ash later prints Segmentation fault from exit status.
steps.why_it_matters: POSIX semantics — parent must observe WIFSIGNALED.

steps.label: Shell continues
steps.what_ir0_does: Parent reaps zombie via wait4. Prompt returns.
steps.why_it_matters: Isolation worked — kernel and shell survived the faulting process.
